provenance.note: District Environment Plan: Kolhapur (2018-19, Environment Department, Government of Maharashtra and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board), which carries no water-balance table: 6 figures the plan states about water, each transcribed with the sentence it was read from and the PDF page it sits on, and 1 of its water action points. Nothing is computed from the plan; a balance is served only where the plan prints one. Review status verified (checked against the document on 2026-09-02).

conventions.figures: value and unit as the plan states them; quote is the sentence verbatim; pdfPage is the viewer's page, printedPage the number printed on it
conventions.waterBalance: null when the plan carries no NGT-template balance; the page says so rather than estimating one
conventions.review: proposed until a person reads every figure against the PDF; then verified with the date
conventions.document: sha256 and byte length of the PDF as retrieved, so a re-posted file is detected; the PDF itself is not mirrored

document.title: District Environment Plan: Kolhapur
document.publisher: Environment Department, Government of Maharashtra and Maharashtra Pollution Control Board
document.editionNote: The label MPCB's listing gives the plans; the PDF metadata dates the file 30 December 2019 and the filename carries 23 June 2021, the date it was posted.
document.template: CPCB model District Environment Plan under NGT O.A. 360 of 2018 (order dated 26 September 2019): a profile table and gap-and-action tables per theme. It is not the NGT water-balance template and carries no demand, supply or deficit table.
quirks: The body introduces the profile as 'General Latur district profile is presented in the Table 1'.
The profile names six rivers while the water-quality section counts two with 80.7 km; both statements are transcribed, neither corrected.
The climate row prints 'Rainfall: 19 to 30 degrees C'.

figures.label: Rivers counted by the water-quality section
figures.detail: 80.7 km of riverine length; the profile table instead names Panchganga, Krishna, Savithri, Veena, Koyna and Gayathri - the contradiction is the plan's, surfaced here.
figures.quote: There are 2 Rivers in Kolhapur district with 80.7km in length.

figures.label: Sewage generated by the 15 ULBs
figures.quote: The 15 ULBs generate about 140.43MLD of sewage with an existing capacity of 86MLD of STP.

figures.label: Installed STP capacity
figures.detail: The plan's own two figures leave 54.43 MLD beyond installed capacity; that arithmetic is ours, not the plan's.
figures.quote: The 15 ULBs generate about 140.43MLD of sewage with an existing capacity of 86MLD of STP.

figures.label: Industrial effluent generation
figures.detail: From 594 industries, treated with the aid of 4 CETPs.
figures.quote: On the other hand industrial effluent are much more regulated wherein 52.5MLD from 594 numbers of industry, limited to the entire district are made to treat almost the entire effluent to the best possible norms as stipulated by their permits, monitored effectively and regularly with the aid of final disposal / treatment in the 4 number of CETP.

figures.label: Common effluent treatment plants
figures.quote: On the other hand industrial effluent are much more regulated wherein 52.5MLD from 594 numbers of industry, limited to the entire district are made to treat almost the entire effluent to the best possible norms as stipulated by their permits, monitored effectively and regularly with the aid of final disposal / treatment in the 4 number of CETP.

actionPoints.text: Map the highest flood line, demarcate and protect flood plains in the ULBs, in light of erratic precipitation in recent years
